claims.quote: A capability is one named action with a contract and a server-side handler.
A contract defines the shared input, output, failures, and metadata.
The RPC client needed the contract without importing server implementation.
A projection converts registered capabilities into an interface.
The interfaces are command line, HTTP, MCP tools, browser RPC, and code mode.
Each interface derives its input and failure definitions from the same schemas.
The browser and the Worker import the same schemas.
A policy requirement names the permissions an operation needs.
A client operation can imply a policy requirement that is supplied when the function is built.
Sam says a binding includes both permissions and environment variables.
A service's configuration and permissions can be declared together before the application runs.
He also describes deriving least-privilege policies: permissions limited to the methods an application uses.
Declare the bindings that give it access to its resources.
An Alchemy Layer can also declare the cloud resources behind a service.
An Alchemy Stack is the infrastructure program that declares cloud resources.
The program carries resource requirements in its context.
Removal must leave no loose resources or broken imports.
A plan model describes infrastructure changes before they are applied.
The engine can show the plan before those values become readable at deployment.
He compares Alchemy's earlier await-based model with a plan model, which describes infrastructure changes before applying them.
He also connects Effect purity with a reviewable plan and a concrete deployment result.
Idempotent recovery can repeat an operation without creating another change.
Tests using real infrastructure check behavior after deployment.
Alchemy reads the same program to deploy and to test.
The compiler can check those relationships before deployment.
Effect tracks required services in its type.
Effects and Layers let the type system track the resource providers a Stack needs.
Sam describes test or development Layers for infrastructure and a type error when code still requires a removed binding.
A cartridge is a package that owns one job and the resources it needs.
Replacing that Layer changes the implementation and its dependencies without changing callers.
A Layer describes how to build services and supply their dependencies.
Use an XState machine for the application's named states, retries, cancellation, or a lifecycle you need to resume or inspect.
Model the states and the events that move between them instead of accumulating booleans whose combinations have no meaning.
The domain read failure remains an explicit machine state.
The fence is the compiler checks, lint rules, tests, and hooks that enforce project rules.
If an enforced check and a paragraph disagree, follow the enforced rule and fix the paragraph.
These rules cannot establish whole-program behavior.
"the whole cloud becomes a library."
Sam calls the cloud a library at 29:50.
Sam describes runtime clients, business logic, infrastructure policies, and deployed resources as related parts of a cloud application.
He says this structure can keep provider implementations out of the runtime bundle.
Sam argues that infrastructure tools can retain ordinary application-code properties such as debugging and tests.
He says constrained conventions make resource generation easier for coding agents.
